newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Sept wage settlements average 1.6 pct. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Canada Sept wage settlements average 1.6 pct. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: Annual wage increases in Canadian collective bargaining agreements reached in September averaged 1.6 percent, up from 1.2 percent in August, the Department of Human Resources Development said on Tuesday.
(Corrects figures for public and private sectors, which had been reversed.)

Wage increases are the average annual percentage increase in base rates -- the wage rate of the lowest paid classification in a bargaining unit -- over the term of the agreement in settlements negotiated during the period shown.
Annual wage increases in collective bargaining agreements reached in the third quarter of 1996 averaged 1.2 percent, up from 0.7 percent in the second quarter.
There were 41 agreements reached in the private sector, covering 65,919 employees who got an average wage increase of 2.0 percent in the quarter.
Public sector employees received an average wage increase of 0.4 percent in the third quarter from 44 agreements covering 65,423 employees.
(For more information on the settlements, contact Human Resources Development's Workplace Information Directorate, at 1-800-567-6866 or 819-997-3117.)
